findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check entirely
findings.body: When a slot falls inside a same-day date override, none of the early-return branches in the find callback fire, so find returns undefined but dateOverrideExist is already true. The following `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` then returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function. Calendar events and existing bookings overlapping the slot are therefore ignored for any host (fixed or round-robin) who has a date override on that day. A round-robin host with a conflict inside their override window stays eligible and can be double-booked. Overrides should narrow availability, not bypass conflict checks; this branch should fall through to the busy check instead of returning true. No test covers a busy time inside an override.

findings.title: Days with more than one date override row reject every slot
findings.body: dateOverrides.find returns the first override for which the callback returns truthy, and the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside that particular override (lines 118-124). With two override rows on the same day, for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00 (the UI stores each range as its own row), a 09:00 slot is inside the first but the second callback returns true, so find returns it and line 130 returns false. The same happens for a 14:00 slot. Every slot on that day is rejected even though slots in both windows are valid. The intended logic is 'available if inside any override on that day', which needs some() with the correct polarity, not find with inverted returns.

findings.title: Split working hours on one weekday remove all slots for that day
findings.body: workingHours.find returns the first entry on the slot's weekday whose range does not contain the slot (the callback returns true when start < startTime or end > endTime). If a host has two ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 (a lunch break, stored as two availability rows), a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 13:00-17:00 entry, and a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 09:00-12:00 entry. The host gets no slots on that day. getSlots already restricts slots to working hours, so this block is either redundant or, as written, breaks split schedules. The existing tests only use one contiguous range per day, so this is not caught.

findings.title: Fixed host's days off are not enforced for round-robin slots
findings.body: The working-hours check only rejects a slot when an entry for the same weekday exists and does not contain it. If a fixed host has no working-hours entry for the slot's weekday (for example a Monday-Friday host and a Saturday slot), find returns undefined and nothing rejects the slot. The slot is generated from the round-robin host's hours, and the fixed host's check then only looks at busy times, so the slot passes. A round-robin event with a fixed host who does not work Saturdays still offers and books Saturday slots with that fixed host. This is the exact problem the PR says it fixes. A fixed host should be treated as unavailable when the slot is not on one of their working days.

findings.title: Shifted override minutes wrap past midnight and land on the wrong day
findings.body: startTime and endTime take only .hour()*60 + .minute() of the offset-shifted instant, which drops the date. The day an override is assigned to comes from the unshifted override.start in the activeOverrides filter, so when the offset pushes the time across midnight the result is attributed to the wrong day. Example: organizer America/New_York, invitee Europe/London, override starting 23:00 UTC on day D. The filter assigns it to London day D. offset = 0 - (-300) = +300, so the shifted time is 04:00 on day D+1, but the code yields 240 and shows 04:00 on day D. Day D+1 loses the override entirely. Evening overrides viewed from zones ahead of the organizer will be misplaced like this. The shifted timestamp should be kept as a full datetime and the day derived from it, not reduced to minutes-of-day.

findings.title: Comparing dayjs objects with === is always false
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares object references, so it is always false. The intended zero-length override check never fires. It should use isSame, or the zero-length case should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: Override day match mixes server-local and UTC formatting
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(...) is in local mode, so it formats in the process timezone, while slotStartTime.format(...) is in UTC (time.utc()). The two strings are compared to decide whether an override applies to the slot's day. On any process not running in UTC, near midnight an override can be matched to the wrong day or not matched at all, which then sends the slot to the working-hours check instead. Both sides should be formatted in UTC.

findings.title: End time is computed from the slot start
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` uses slotStartTime, so `end` equals `start` and the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison tests the slot start rather than the slot end. A slot that starts inside the working window and runs past its end is not rejected here. The variable should use slotEndTime.

findings.title: Optional override timeZone is passed to tz() with no fallback
findings.body: TimeRange.timeZone was just made optional, but getSlots passes override.timeZone straight into .tz() without a fallback, even though organizerTimeZone is already in scope in this function. When timeZone is undefined, dayjs falls back to the default or the process local zone, so the organizer offset is computed against the wrong zone without any error. The fallback should be organizerTimeZone, or the code should fail loudly.

findings.title: toHaveTimeSlots passes when fewer slots than expected are returned
findings.body: The matcher iterates over the actual slots only (.every over schedule.slots[date]) and compares each to expectedSlots[index]. Missing trailing expected slots are never detected, so an assertion expecting four override slots passes if only one matching slot is returned. Every new override assertion depends on this matcher, so regressions that remove slots (multiple override rows on one day, fixed host days off, split working hours) would go unnoticed. The matcher should also assert the lengths match.

findings.title: Headline scenarios of the PR have no test coverage
findings.body: The PR's main change, fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events, has no test. The only new test is an extra assertion in the single-host override test, which has no hosts, no busy times, and one override row. None of the regressions in this change are exercised: a busy time inside an override, two override rows on the same day, a split working-hours day, or a fixed host without working hours on the slot's weekday. Tests should cover each of these, and the round-robin plus fixed-host override case the PR describes.

findings.title: New timeZone field on TimeRange is undocumented and its semantics are load-bearing
findings.body: The new optional timeZone is added without a comment. The code relies on an undocumented convention: override start and end are treated as organizer wall-clock time carried in their UTC fields, and the organizer's offset is applied in both lib/slots.ts and checkIfIsAvailable. Nothing in this type says which timezone the field refers to or how start and end should be interpreted, so a future change to getUserAvailability could break the override logic silently.
